_meta._comment: Actions that resolve one character's check against other characters, for Mutants & Masterminds 4e (Open Game Content). Numeric game-mechanical facts and short paraphrased labels only. Consumed by mm_companion.core.data_loader; core.rules.impress and core.rules.targeting interpret these generically rather than hardcoding the action in Python.
_meta.impressNote: The Impress action. An interaction skill check sets the DC each target resists; the degree by which a target fails picks a rung of the chosen impression's ladder.
_meta.skillsNote: Skill ids (skills.json) an impression may be made with. Any impression pairs with any of them: the impression decides what success does, the skill decides what is rolled.
_meta.resistNote: What a target resists with. sameSkill offers the skill the impresser used; skills and resistances name further options by id. 'Use highest' picks the best of them on the target's own sheet.
_meta.groupPenaltyNote: Applied once to the impress check when it is aimed at more than one target (a group impression).
_meta.impressionsNote: Each impression: an id, a display name, an optional suggested skill (preselected when it is chosen), an optional advantage id the impresser must have, and an outcomes ladder in the same shape as an effect's resistanceOutcomes (one rung per degree of failure, the last covering every deeper one). A rung's parameters map a condition id to the parameter it is applied with; '{source}' is replaced by the impresser's name.
_meta.modifiersNote: The situational modifiers the GM sets on an impress check. label is the short caption the control wears; hint (optional) is the longer explanation shown behind a "?". kind 'toggle' is a checkbox worth value; toggles sharing an exclusive group cannot both be on. kind 'slider' runs from min to max in steps of step and is worth its position.
_meta.areaNote: Area attacks. modifiers lists the modifier ids that make an effect an area effect; their shape, applications and spread config is read by core.rules.area. A creature in the area makes a resistance check (dodge, a resistance key) against dcBase + the area rank; making it gives Resistance, which halves the rank they then resist the effect at (halve: 'up' rounds up). The one creature targeted directly and hit by the attack check makes no Dodge check and resists the full rank.
_meta.areaShapesNote: How each shape's size reads. {d} is the measurement of the shape's distance rank (baseDistanceRank, plus one per application past the first); {n} is a Shapeable area's spaces (the effect rank, doubled per application past the first).
_meta.areaEvasionNote: An advantage that helps against areas: dodgeBonus is added to the Dodge check, and at negateAtRank or more ranks a made Dodge check means no effect at all.
_meta.areaFreeUseNote: Any attack may be used as an area at the table without buying the extra (the GM's call, as for an attacker far larger than its target). Its area rank is capped at the Power Level when freeUsePlCap is true, raised by whatever the wielder's size adds to the effect, as the rank cap is.
_meta.areaWorstOfNote: An effect resisted by either of two traits is resisted with the better one, unless a modifier choice listed in worstOf says the target takes the worse (modifier id, config key, chosen value). This is how the GM's table rolls a creature nobody plays against an Alternate Resistance's worst of two.
_meta.areaCoverNote: Cover a creature has from the area's origin, as the GM sets it per creature: value is added to its Dodge check. Total cover keeps a creature out of the area entirely, so it is simply not included.
_meta.combatNote: Combat maneuvers and the other combat actions, offered from the roller's Actions popup. menu is the popup's sections in order, each naming action ids defined under actions. limits are the attack maneuvers' two caps: a shift is at most maxShift, may not take the penalised value below floor, and (doubleCap) may not more than double the bonused value.
_meta.combatActionsNote: Each action: id, name, an optional short caption for its tile (the name when absent), an icon key (a drawing the app ships; an unknown key draws a generic one), a tooltip, and a kind. kind 'maneuver' shifts up to X between two values (bonus, penalty: attack_check, effect_rank or defense) and may leave a lasting condition (a conditions.json id taking X as its amount). 'self' acts on the actor, 'targeted' on someone else, 'loader' loads a check into the roller, 'attack' makes an attack, 'builtin' is run by the app's own window or the dice (Impress, Area, the team actions, Reroll). needsAttack: the action works on an attack loaded into the roller. gmOnly: offered on the GM's roller only. A self or loader action (or each of its options, whose fields override the action's) may carry: line (a caption: it rides on the next roll as a line on the roller's lane), tone (benefit/hindrance, the line's colour), attackModifier, rollTwice (roll twice, keep the higher), dc and criticalHit (every hit is a critical), slam and fullSpeed (with the action's slamRules: rankBonus, fullSpeedBonus, selfResistance, halveSelf), kill (degrees, condition: that many degrees of failure on a damage save land the condition instead); or, taking effect at once, applies ([{condition, amount?, temporary?}]), removes ([condition ids]), and check ({kind: ability/skill/speed, trait, dc}, loaded into the roller) whose success sheds clears. requires / refusedBy name a condition the actor must have / must not. recovery {from: condition ids most severe first, fatigue} is what Recover may shed. gmRuns is why a player's tile is greyed: the GM runs it. A targeted action (Aid, Feint, Trick) carries targeted: check ('attack' — the attack loaded, or {kind, trait} as above), and either dc (against a fixed DC) or resist (the target's best of [{kind, trait}], opposing the check's total), and ally (Aid: the outcome lands on an ally, the target being the opponent). wins and losses (on the action or an option) are ladders of {degrees, applies}: the deepest entry the actor's degrees of success (or of failure) reach lands. Each applies entry may name on (target or ally; target when absent) and against (actor or target): the condition's parameter is that one's name, the creature its 'opposing' rule is about. A targeted check may also be a list (the actor's best of them), and 'damage' (the attack's Damage rank); the dc may be 'defense' (the target's Defense: Grab, Trip, Disarm, Smash) or {base, kind, trait} (a base plus one of the target's traits: Escape). opposed {check, resist} is a second stage once the attack has hit: the actor's best of check against the target's best of resist (Grab, Trip, Disarm). on may also be actor (Grab's Holding); a rung may carry removes ([{condition, on?, against?}]) and text (what the app does not track, said in the history; {actor} and {target} are the two names). reaction (Block) is what taking a self action again does while its condition is on: it loads a check with the attack picked, step more for each count of the condition past the first, and adds one to the count.
_meta.provenance: Area Effect extra (targeting, shapes, Dodge resistance), cover against areas and the Evasion advantage: Mutants & Masterminds core rules, Powers, Advantages and Action and Adventure chapters. Impress action, impression effects and impress check modifiers: Mutants & Masterminds core rules, Action and Adventure chapter. Mechanics only; labels paraphrased. Combat maneuvers and combat actions (Accurate, All-Out, Defensive, Power, Finishing and Surprise Attack; Aid, Aim, Block, Catch, Charge, Defend, Disarm, Drop Prone, Escape, Feint, Grab, Recover, Smash, Stand, Trick and Trip): Mutants & Masterminds core rules, Action and Adventure chapter.

modifiers.label: Simple action
modifiers.hint: Impressing as a simple action rather than a standard one.

modifiers.label: Full action
modifiers.hint: Taking a full action over the attempt.

modifiers.label: Earlier attempts
modifiers.hint: Each earlier attempt to Impress in this scene.

modifiers.label: Mood
modifiers.hint: The prevailing mood: against the impression (minus) or matching it (plus).

modifiers.label: Position
modifiers.hint: The impresser's position: at a disadvantage (minus), or at an advantage or making an impressive display (plus).

modifiers.label: Threatening
modifiers.hint: Something violent or threatening backs the attempt.

modifiers.label: Target hurt
modifiers.hint: The target has suffered damage or a similar condition.

modifiers.label: Complications
modifiers.hint: The attempt plays on a target's complications.

actions.name: Accurate Attack
actions.caption: Accurate
actions.tooltip: Trade effect for accuracy: up to +5 on the attack check, the same amount off the effect rank.

actions.name: All-Out Attack
actions.caption: All-Out
actions.tooltip: Throw caution aside: up to +5 on the attack check, the same amount off your Defense until your next turn.

actions.name: Defensive Attack
actions.caption: Defensive
actions.tooltip: Attack with care: up to +5 Defense until your next turn, the same amount off your attack checks.

actions.name: Power Attack
actions.caption: Power
actions.tooltip: Hit harder but less surely: up to +5 on the effect rank, the same amount off the attack check.

actions.name: Finishing Attack
actions.caption: Finishing
actions.tooltip: Attack a defenseless target normally, against DC 10, instead of hitting it automatically: a hit is a critical hit. With intent to kill, three or more degrees of failure on the damage are fatal.
actions.line: vs DC 10, a hit is critical

actions.name: Surprise Attack
actions.caption: Surprise
actions.tooltip: The target is caught off guard: vulnerable, or defenseless if completely surprised.
actions.gmRuns: The GM grants a surprise attack: ask them, and they make the target vulnerable (or defenseless, if completely surprised).

actions.name: Aid
actions.tooltip: Help an ally against an opponent: an attack check against DC 10 gives them +2 (+5 on three degrees) on their next attack on that opponent, or to their Defense against its next attack.

actions.name: Aim
actions.tooltip: Take careful aim: roll your next attack twice and keep the better. Lost if your next standard action is not that attack.

actions.name: Attack
actions.tooltip: Make an attack: pick one, then (optionally) the target.

actions.name: Block
actions.tooltip: Ready yourself to block close attacks until your next turn. When one comes, take Block again: your close attack check against the attacker's result, -2 for each block after the first this round.

actions.name: Catch
actions.tooltip: Catch something thrown or falling: an Agility check against DC 10.

actions.name: Charge
actions.tooltip: Rush at least a short way in a straight line and make a close attack at -2. Or slam into the target: more damage, but you resist the impact yourself.

options.name: Slam Attack after a full-speed move

actions.name: Defend
actions.tooltip: Spend your turn on defense: a bonus to your Defense until your next turn.

actions.name: Disarm
actions.tooltip: Knock an item out of someone's hands: an attack at -2 against their Defense, then your attack's Damage rank against their Strength. Win, and they drop it.

actions.name: Drop Prone
actions.caption: Prone
actions.tooltip: Drop to the ground.

actions.name: Escape
actions.tooltip: Break free of a hold: your Strength or Sleight of Hand against the grab's effect DC (10 + the grabber's Strength). With two or more degrees you can also move.

wins.text: {actor} may also move up to their speed rank -1

actions.name: Feint
actions.tooltip: Mislead an opponent with a false attack: your attack check against the best of their combat skills, Deception or Insight. A win leaves them vulnerable to your next attack.

options.name: Feint, as a simple action at -5

actions.name: Grab
actions.tooltip: Seize someone: a close attack against their Defense, then your Strength against their Strength or Dodge. One degree holds them (restrained), two binds them; while you hold them you are hindered and vulnerable.

actions.name: Impress
actions.tooltip: Use an interaction skill to impose a condition on someone.

actions.name: Recover
actions.tooltip: Catch your breath: +2 Defense until your next turn, and a recovery check for your worst damage condition, or shake off your worst fatigue, or a new resistance check against an impression or an Affliction on you. Recovering this way works once per conflict scene.

actions.name: Smash
actions.tooltip: Damage or break something another character holds or wears: an attack at -2 against their Defense (-5 against a hand-held or smaller object). A hit deals the attack's Damage to the object.

wins.text: the attack's Damage lands on what {target} holds or wears

options.name: Smash a hand-held or smaller object (-5)

actions.name: Stand
actions.tooltip: Get up from prone: a difficult check, or stand slowly and be hindered.

options.name: Stand slowly: hindered until your next turn

actions.name: Trick
actions.tooltip: Outwit an opponent: Deception against their Deception or Insight. A win leaves them heedless of the risk of acting against you; losing badly gives them +5 on their next attack on you.

actions.name: Trip
actions.tooltip: Knock someone down: a close attack against their Defense, then your close attack bonus or Strength against their Strength or Dodge. Win, and they are prone.

wins.text: {target} may be thrown a space further for each degree past the first

actions.name: Area Attack
actions.caption: Area
actions.tooltip: Use an attack on an area: everyone in it makes a Dodge check.

actions.name: Team Attack
actions.caption: Team attack
actions.tooltip: Call a team attack on one target: anyone at the table joins with their next attack, maneuvers and all, and you resolve it. A group's own menu still rolls a squad at once.

actions.name: Team Check
actions.caption: Team check
actions.tooltip: The members of a group help their leader with a check.

actions.name: Group Check
actions.caption: Group check
actions.tooltip: Everyone in a group makes the same check; the group succeeds if half of them do.

actions.name: Reroll
actions.tooltip: Reroll your last roll with the same bonus, penalty and DC. A result of 1–10 gets +10, so it lands on 11–20.

actions.name: Ask to Roll
actions.caption: Ask
actions.tooltip: Ask the table to roll a trait: it lands in everyone's history with a button that rolls it on their own sheet.

actions.name: Take 10
actions.tooltip: Make the check now as a routine one: the die counts as a 10, so there is no natural 1 or 20. For a check made without pressure. Takes whatever is loaded, with the modifier and the DC set (Ctrl+T).
